speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: They all come here kinda wanting to be an American entrepreneur. So they're always like, can you can you can you help me tell my story like this? I'll give me, like, a video or an example. speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: Like, they have fear coming here. They're trying to stand out. They're trying to find their unique positioning. But oftentimes, when we get into their story, their story is so fascinating. It's usually...
zh: 就像，他们带着恐惧来到这里。他们想脱颖而出。他们想找到自己的独特定位。但很多时候，当我们深入他们的故事时，他们的故事如此迷人。通常是……

speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: There's usually a ton of, like, obstacles for them to even get to, you know, MIT, obviously. They come from, you know, a lot of backgrounds that, you know, took a lot of resilience, a lot of overcoming, And there's this... All this gold in their story that they're basically trying to hide. zh: 通常有大量的障碍要克服，才能走到，你知道，MIT，显然。他们来自，你知道，各种背景，这些背景需要很多韧性、很多克服困难的经历。而他们故事里有这种……所有这些宝藏，而他们基本上是在试图隐藏它。这非常……很多过程就是在努力提取出那种独特的定位。

speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: And that really is what sort of informed, you know, what I'm calling right now a little bit around narrative intelligence, but it's really about how extract your unique self into your story and evolve it in real time. zh: 而这真正塑造了我现在称之为「叙事智能」（narrative intelligence）的概念，但它本质上是关于如何把你的独特自我提取到你的故事中，并实时地演变它。因为对于 AI，每个人，你知道，既兴奋又恐惧。所以存在这种不断的来回摇摆。因此，如何持续适应，就是我目前所有的教练和工作中贯穿始终的东西。

speaker: Reef Frerichs

speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: There's been different people that have looked at it. zh: 有不同的人研究过它。而且真的，我记得我看到的那篇文章大约是 MIT 和哈佛的不同工程师试图学会如何彼此交流。于是他们围绕它成立了一个小组。这让我开始思考，好的。鉴于当下 AI 的时代，还有什么东西在这里？

speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: And so as I started, you know, interviewing people and working with people, I started thinking what what could become more real time around, like, what could become narrative intelligence? zh: 所以当我开始，你知道，采访别人并与别人共事时，我开始思考什么可能变得更实时，比如，什么可以成为叙事智能？讲故事显然有它的位置，对于领导者或正在融资的创始人、给客户做路演来说。但很多时候，讲故事的人卡在故事里，不去演变它。所以那时我开始想，就像，初创公司创始人每天都面临变化。有新信息，还有新的受众。

speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: And how do you just continuously evolve it? So that's sort of where I I started. So I I pitched it. I did my first talk at at South by Southwest last year. And I was so nervous.

en: I was going in there. I was in the green room, and I remember the guy from, like, Ted Lasso, if you've seen that show, is in there. And he's sitting there, and I'm, so nervous. I'm, oh my god. There's, like, people around here.

speaker: Reef Frerichs

speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: So I started peeking outside the door going, gosh, I wonder if anybody's gonna show up in this room. And luckily, it was it was sold out. We... It was, like, 50 people. So I'm not talking like a 400 person theater, but it was a really good conversation.
zh: 所以我开始从门缝往外偷看，心想，天哪，不知道会不会有人来这个场子。幸运的是，它满座了。我们……大概 50 个人。所以我说的不是一个 400 人的剧场，但那是一场非常好的对话。

speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: A lot of interesting perspectives, questions, curious about what you were just asking. What is this narrative intelligence and how are you, you know, coaching it? zh: 我们那里有一位曾经是 NASA 顶层人物之一的人，他说，我现在正试图改变我的职业，我正试图过渡到人生的下一个阶段。所以这真正告诉我的是，它有点像经典的英雄之旅。如果你熟悉 Joseph Campbell，或者基本上每一部电影里都有的那个。是啊。每部电影，它有点像我们全都活在那个英雄之旅中。你知道，我们在……

speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: We had one guy there who was one of the top guys at NASA, and he was like, I'm trying to change my career now, and I'm trying to transition in this next stage of life. speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: You know, whether it's the call, we're being called into some adventure or action, or we're going through the threshold, or whether we're turning back home or we're trying to get back to our true self. There's all these kind of periods we go through. So as I dove deeper into it, I pulled a lot of my acting that I coaching I received. I was fortunate to train with some of the top acting coaches in LA. And then coaching, psychology, neuroscience, I started trying to pull, extract different things from it.
zh: 你知道，无论是被召唤，我们被召唤进入某场冒险或行动，还是我们正在跨越门槛，还是我们要转返回家，或者我们正在努力回到真实的自我。我们会经历所有这些阶段。所以当我更深入地钻研它时，我提取了很多我接受过的表演训练和教练。我很幸运在 LA 和一些顶级的表演教练训练过。然后是教练技术、心理学、神经科学，我开始试着从中提取不同的东西。

speaker: Reef Frerichs
en: And what I really came up with is a three step process, which is own, author, and act. You know, show up each day and own where you're at, whether you like it or not or whether you're neutral on it, but own where you are in your journey. You know, look at ways that you can extract the learnings forward and then author this next chapter, this next phase for you. It could be that week, that quarter, that next milestone, but learn to author it. And what I found in the coaching was a lot of times it required a little reframing of your story.
